commit.message:
Use the suffix of a stale NewState instead of asserting on it

A backup in state transfer accepted any NewState as the answer to its
current GetState and asserted that the reply started at its op number.
Nothing ties a reply to the request it answers, so when the network
delayed or replayed a GetState from an earlier transfer, the primary's
reply to that copy arrived during a later transfer, started before the
backup's current op number, and tripped the assertion. The paper leaves
out "filtering of duplicate messages"; this is one of the cases it
covers.

on_new_state now compares the reply's range with the log. In a single
view the overlapping entries are identical, so a reply that starts at or
before the current op number and ends beyond it is still useful: append
only the entries past the log and finish the transfer. A reply that
starts past the log or ends inside it brings nothing usable, so the
backup keeps waiting for another. The commit number in a stale reply
can be lower than the backup's own, so that check becomes a lower
bound.

Add a cluster test where a backup's GetState is replayed, its next
transfer's GetState is lost, and the reply to the replayed copy arrives
during the second transfer covering both the old and the missing
entries.

Found by the simulator at commit 7cf58fa with:

    SEED=8711571497407488070 cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- --lite

which panicked at src/replica.rs:275 on tick 57 with op_number_start 8
against op number 13. With this fix the seed no longer fails a safety
property; it stops with "no state convergence: pending request"
because the last PrepareOk messages were lost and nothing retransmits.
